item.title: Political debate over AI intensifies amid warnings about ‘catastrophic risk’
item.description:
# Political debate over AI intensifies amid warnings about ‘catastrophic risk’ The debate around [artificial intelligence](https://www.cnn.com/business/tech/ai-news-artificial-intelligence-updates) is ramping up in Washington, with Democratic lawmakers sounding alarms on the dangers they say the technology poses and Republican leaders suggesting those concerns are inflated and secondary to winning the AI race with China.
Meanwhile, former President Barack Obama told Democrats to make [artificial intelligence](https://www.cnn.com/business/tech/ai-news-artificial-intelligence-updates) regulation a central part of their agenda during a private fundraiser Thursday, warning that the technology could be dangerous “if we don’t get on top of it.”
Concerns over the rapid acceleration of AI reached a fever pitch after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei [wrote](https://www.cnn.com/2026/09/12/tech/anthropic-ceo-essay-ai) in a 3,800-word essay Saturday that the race to develop artificial intelligence is in dire need of a slowdown.
“President Obama is correct that decisive action must be taken on Artificial Intelligence,” he said, adding, “In the majority, we will move urgently on this issue with a legislative response that recognizes the importance of American companies continuing to lead in the Artificial Intelligence area, while putting in place meaningful guardrails that protect the American people from bad actors and the very real damage that can be done to humanity.”

BERLIN/BRUSSELS/LONDON, Sept 14 (Reuters) - Germany on Monday said halting the development ​of artificial intelligence systems was not a "viable option" for Europe, as the region's governments responded to a call ‌from a top tech executive to slow the AI push and devote more time to testing.
The ministry said AI systems capable of [breaking out of test environments](https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/openai-agents-hijacked-german-website-previously-undisclosed-ai-breakout-this-2026-09-04/) and accessing other systems on ​their own — as seen in July, when OpenAI agents hacked open-source platform [Hugging Face](https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/fallout-openai-hugging-face-hack-2026-07-29/) — would represent "an entirely new threat scenario" requiring a new policy response.
